note:
Header banner for /pages/contact. The hero has NO IMAGE AT ALL today — verified on the live theme 2026-08-30: templates/page.contact.json section `hero` (image-with-text-overlay) carries no `image` and no `mobile_image`, so it paints flat #1A1A1A at overlay_opacity 100 with centred white type. Same for /pages/shipping-returns. These are the last two pages on the site without a photograph.

Malcolm's brief, 2026-08-30: 'similar to the main menu contact image tile. A close up of a dermatologist smiling - talking to a client.'

The tile he means is CONTACT-A-listening (gpt_image), chosen 2026-08-22 from the 24-image dermatologist batch and live as skingenetix-dermatologist-skin-consultation-client-conversation.jpg. Its shape is the thing to keep: ONE clinician large in frame, the client present only as a soft out-of-focus mass in the near foreground. That is what survived the downscale to a 232px tile, and it is also what survives a 440px banner band. The brief here changes two things and nothing else — the expression becomes speaking-and-smiling rather than listening, and the frame becomes 2.4:1 instead of square.

GEOMETRY. Generated at 3072x1280 (2.4:1), the page-break band spec. The winner then goes through scripts/extend-banner-canvas.py to ~4.42:1 so full height survives a 1920 viewport — the box is a fixed PIXEL height (375/400/440px full-bleed), not an aspect ratio, so surplus width is croppable margin rather than waste.

TYPE ZONE IS THE LEFT 45 PERCENT, stated as a measured fraction of frame width because a body anchor does not hold across suppliers. Matches /pages/the-science and the collection banners so the site reads as one system. ⚠️ The subject therefore sits RIGHT, which is what object-position: right center wants — but see the memory note: the right-pin zooms the subject into the copy between 700 and 1199px, and the answer there is a capped text column plus a local gradient, never a heavier section overlay.

⚠️ The left 45 percent is specified as CONTINUOUS ROOM, softly out of focus and evenly lit — deliberately not as 'quiet and almost empty'. That exact phrasing produced a hard black bar across a model's forehead on all five engines on the FAQ macro. Say what reaches the edges; never describe a background you do not want.

NO REFERENCE IMAGE IS SENT (class B). Nothing branded is in frame, and a reference pulls the framing back to its own camera distance — the opposite of what a close two-shot needs. For the same reason no product is described: a described product gets drawn, and a drawn product gets an invented label.

Text is negated hard. A white coat invites an embroidered name, and an embroidered name on a banner is an invented brand. Class B has no branding in frame, so FLUX.2 is allowed to route — but it is the one engine that prints numbers unasked, so check its candidates at full size.

defaults.negative_global: text, lettering, embroidered name, printed name tag, pocket badge, logo, brand mark, watermark, signature, border, collage, multi-panel, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, plastic waxy airbrushed skin, extra fingers, malformed hands, stethoscope, clipboard, medical chart, signage on the wall, framed artwork, wall poster

slots.title: Clinician speaking and smiling, client soft in the near foreground (the tile shape, widened)
slots.prompt:
A photorealistic wide editorial photograph, 2.4:1 letterbox format, of a consultation between a skin clinician and her client, shot as a close two-shot.

The clinician is a woman in her early forties with warm mid-brown skin and dark hair drawn back, wearing a plain white cotton clinical coat over a soft grey top. The coat is completely plain — no pocket badge, no embroidery, no printed characters of any kind anywhere on it. Her head occupies the right side of the frame, from about 0.58 to 0.86 of the frame width and from about 0.14 to 0.72 of the frame height. She is turned about twenty degrees away from the camera toward the left of frame, talking to the client and smiling warmly as she speaks — lips parted mid-sentence, the smile reaching the eyes, an open and unhurried expression. Her eyes are in sharp focus.

In the near foreground at the right edge, the back of the client's head and one shoulder are visible, cropped by the right edge of the frame, entering from the bottom edge and reaching up to about 0.60 of the frame height and inward to about 0.94 of the frame width. The client is rendered soft and thoroughly out of focus so the clinician's face is unambiguously the subject; only the outline of hair and shoulder reads, no facial features.

The clinician shows real, unretouched skin — visible pores, fine lines at the outer eye, faint natural colour variation — lit so that texture is present without being emphasised. Her face is not smoothed.

Lighting is a large, soft, north-facing window source from the front-left, giving gentle directional modelling across her face and no hard shadow edges.

The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 0.45 of frame width, is the continuation of the same consultation room, thrown well out of focus: a clean pale interior of warm off-white and soft grey, evenly lit at a mid tone, holding gentle continuous gradation with no dark band, no vignette and no abrupt change of tone anywhere. It is soft and simple enough for a headline to sit on it unaided, but it is a real room and not an empty void. Nothing in it reads as a recognisable object, and there is no signage, artwork, character or symbol anywhere in the picture. The room fills the frame all the way to the top edge, the bottom edge and the left edge.

Colour is calm and clinical-warm: white, warm off-white, soft grey, and natural skin tones only. Shot on a full-frame camera with an 85mm lens at f/2.0, natural colour, no filter, magazine-quality editorial photography.
slots.negative_extra: no second clinician, no visible face on the foreground client

Nothing in it reads as a recognisable object, and there is no signage, artwork, character or symbol anywhere in the picture. The room reaches the top, bottom and left edges of the frame.
